Single quotes are valid in URIs and query strings, so a URL on the embeddable_host with `' onmouseover='...` in its query can break out of the href attribute; the host check in TopicRetriever compares only URI(...).host, and the fetch still succeeds on a valid page. judged_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — Unescaped `url` is interpolated into `#{url}` inside a raw_html post; an attacker-chosen embed_url like `http:///?x'onmouseover='alert(1)` parses fine with URI (single quote is unreserved), the host check passes, the page fetch returns 200, and the payload becomes stored XSS in both the iframe and the main forum topic.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the diff appends `contents << "...#{url}..."` and then creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. The diff also changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == ...[:raw_html]`, and the embed view renders posts with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The only URL validation in `import` is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, so an attacker-controlled URL containing a single quote (e.g. in the query string) can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute and inject arbitrary attributes/HTML, producing stored XSS in the topic and iframe.
